title: Holidays and Traditions
description: Ten short stories about birthdays, a wedding, Thanksgiving, the Fourth of July, Halloween, New Year's and other American customs.

lessons.title: Lily Turns Seven
lessons.summary: Lily turns seven, and her mother and sister give her a simple party under the big tree.
lessons.text:
Lily is a little girl. On Saturday, she turned seven. Her mother wanted a simple party at home: a few friends, some games and a cake. "A simple party is the best party," her mother said.

On Friday night, Lily's big sister, Emma, helped their mother. They put a long table outside, under the big tree. They put white paper on the table. Then they hung paper stars on the tree. Emma also hung a sign over the table. It said, "Lily is 7!"

On Saturday morning, Emma did her little sister's hair. She worked on the hair for half an hour. "Your hair looks amazing," Emma said. Lily looked at her hair and was very happy.

At 2, seven friends came to the party. First, the children played hide and seek. Emma closed her eyes, and the children ran. One boy went behind the tree. Two girls went under the table. Emma found them all. They played hide and seek again and again.

Then their mother brought out the cake. It had a big 7 on it. Everyone said, "Happy birthday, Lily!" Her father gave her a present. It was a book about a little dog.

At night, the friends went home. Lily and her sister stayed under the tree, and Emma read the new book to her. It started with "Once upon a time." Lily always loved stories that started with "Once upon a time." At the end, Lily said, "Thank you, Emma. It was an amazing day."

Questions:
How old did Lily turn on Saturday?
Lily turned seven.
What kind of party did her mother want?
Her mother wanted a simple party at home.
What did Emma and her mother hang on the tree?
They hung paper stars on the tree.
What did Emma do on Saturday morning?
Emma did her little sister's hair.
What game did the children play?
They played hide and seek.

lessons.title: Anna and Mark's Wedding
lessons.summary: Anna and Mark get married in a small church by the river and dance with their families.
lessons.text:
Anna and Mark met at college. They were together for five years. Then, in June, they had their wedding.

The wedding was in a small old church near the river. Their entire families came. Anna's parents came, and Mark's parents came. Their brothers, friends and old teachers came too. The church was full.

Anna wore a long white dress. Her father walked with her to the front of the church. Mark was there, next to the minister. The minister was an old man with a kind voice. He spoke about love and respect. "Love is not only a feeling," the minister said. "Love is also respect. Respect each other every day." Anna and Mark listened. Then Mark put a ring on Anna's hand. Everyone stood up and clapped.

After the church, the entire group walked to a park by the river. A professional took photos of the family. He was very good. He knew where to stand and where to look. "He is a real professional," said Anna's mother.

Then the music started. It was pop music, and everyone wanted to dance. Anna and Mark had the first dance. Then their parents joined them. Mark's little brother tried to dance too. Everyone danced by the river until late.

Two months later, the photos came in a big album. As a little girl, Anna liked to touch the old pictures in her parents' album. Now she had her own album. She touched the first photo and smiled.

Questions:
Where was the wedding?
The wedding was in a small old church near the river.
What did the minister speak about?
He spoke about love and respect.
Who took photos of the family?
A professional took photos of the family.
What kind of music did they dance to?
They danced to pop music.
What came two months later?
The photos came in a big album.

lessons.title: Food for Thanksgiving
lessons.summary: Tom and his father help a local organization sort food for poor families before Thanksgiving.
lessons.text:
Every year in November, a small organization in Tom's town helps poor families at Thanksgiving. This year, the organization started a campaign. The campaign had a simple idea: "Bring one bag of food for a family."

Tom's school got involved. His teacher told the class about the campaign. "Many families in our town are poor," she said. "Some families cannot buy a big Thanksgiving meal. We can help them."

The response was amazing. Students brought rice, soup and many other things. Parents got involved too. At the end of the campaign, the school had double the food of last year. Double! "What a response!" said the teacher.

On Saturday, Tom and his father went to the organization. The staff was very friendly. There were only five people on the staff, so they needed help. A woman from the staff showed them a big room full of food. "We have to sort all this," she said. "We cannot do it without you."

Tom and his father worked all morning. They sorted the food into boxes. Each box had the same things in it. Tom sorted the soup, and his father sorted the rice. At the end, they had 200 boxes.

On Wednesday, the families came to receive their boxes. Each family received one box. A mother with three children received a box from Tom. "Thank you," she said. "Happy Thanksgiving." Tom felt very happy.

Questions:
What did the organization start this year?
It started a campaign to bring food for families.
Who got involved?
Tom's school and the parents got involved.
What was the response like?
The response was amazing.
How much food did the school have at the end?
The school had double the food of last year.
What did Tom and his father do on Saturday?
They sorted the food into boxes.
When did the families receive their boxes?
They received their boxes on Wednesday.

lessons.title: Football After the Big Meal
lessons.summary: The Miller family eats a big Thanksgiving meal and then plays a friendly game of football.
lessons.text:
Every Thanksgiving, the Miller family eats a big dinner together. This year, there were 12 people at the table. Not all of them were related. Sara, a friend of the family, came too. She is not related to the Millers, but she comes every year.

The food was very rich. There was turkey, and there were three kinds of pie. Jack ate and ate. Then he pushed his food away. "I couldn't eat any more," he said. He had a little pain in his side. "That pain is from all the rich food," his mother said.

His father said, "Every Thanksgiving, I gain 2 pounds." His mother answered, "And this year you are going to gain 3!" Everyone at the table started to laugh.

After the food, the family went to the park for their football game. Jack's uncle, Dan, is a football coach at a high school. He is a serious coach at work. But on Thanksgiving, he is not serious at all. "This game is just for fun," Coach Dan said. "No pushing, please!"

They made two teams. Sara said, "I haven't played football in 30 years!" But she played, and she played well. She got the ball and ran with it. Nobody could stop her. Jack couldn't believe it. His team won by one point.

When they came home, it was dark. The pain in Jack's side was gone. "I haven't had so much fun all year," Jack said. Then he ate one more piece of pie.

Questions:
Was everyone at the table related?
No, Sara was not related to the family.
Why did Jack have a pain in his side?
He had a pain from all the rich food.
What does Dan do at work?
He is a football coach at a high school.
Is Coach Dan serious on Thanksgiving?
No, he is not serious at all on Thanksgiving.
Who got the ball and ran with it?
Sara got the ball and ran with it.

lessons.title: Fireworks Over the River
lessons.summary: Ben and his father go to the town's July 4 party in Central Park and watch the fireworks.
lessons.text:
Every year on July 4, the town council has a big party in Central Park. The park is in the central part of town, next to the river. The council has had this party for more than a century. "A century is 100 years," Ben's father said. "That's a long time."

This year, Ben went to the party with his father. It was a very hot day. At 3, it was 95 degrees. "95 degrees!" said Ben. "That's too hot." His father gave him some water.

There were American flags all over the park. Ben's father showed him a flag. "Do you know what the stars represent?" he asked. "Each star represents one state. There are 50 stars, so there are 50 states."

At 6, a woman from the town council stood up in front of the people. "Can I have your attention, please?" she said. Everyone gave her their attention. She asked all the people from the army to stand up. Ben noticed that his father stood up. His father was in the army for four years, before Ben was born. Ben noticed that many old men and women stood up too. "Thank you," the woman said to them. Everyone said, "Thank you!"

Later, the hot day became cooler. A light wind came from the river. Ben noticed the wind in the trees. It was only 80 degrees now.

When it was dark, the fireworks started over the river. The dark sky was full of red, white and blue lights. Ben looked at his father. "This is the best July 4 ever," Ben said.

Questions:
Where does the town council have the party?
The council has the party in Central Park.
How hot was it at 3?
It was 95 degrees.
What does each star on the flag represent?
Each star represents one state.
What did Ben notice at 6?
He noticed that his father stood up.
When did the fireworks start?
The fireworks started when it was dark.

lessons.title: Two Little Animals
lessons.summary: On Halloween, Max and his little sister Zoe dress as animals and visit the houses on their street.
lessons.text:
Max is 8, and his sister Zoe is 5. This year on Halloween, they both wanted to be animals. Max wanted to be a bear. Zoe wanted to be a dog. Their mother made the two animal costumes.

Before dinner, Zoe played outside in her costume. She fell on the ground and damaged it. One part came off. "Don't worry," her father said. "I can fix it." He fixed it in 10 minutes. "Look," he said. "There's no damage now."

When it got dark, the two animals went out with their father. He used the light on his cell phone. They went from house to house. At each door, they said, "Trick or treat!"

At the first house, an old lady opened the door. "Hey, look at these animals!" said the lady. "A bear and a little dog!" The lady gave them some candy.

The next house had a Halloween scene in front of it. There were big black animals, a dark tree and red lights. Zoe did not want to go to the door. But Max wanted to prove that he was a big boy. He walked past the scene to the door, and he came back with candy. He proved that he was a big boy. Then Zoe looked at the scene again. It was not so bad.

At the end of the street, Zoe could not find her candy. They searched for it. Their father searched with his cell phone light. Max found it under a tree. "Hey, here it is!" he said.

In the end, the two animals managed to visit 15 houses. At home, they put all the candy on the table.

Questions:
What animals did Max and Zoe want to be?
Max wanted to be a bear, and Zoe wanted to be a dog.
Who fixed Zoe's costume?
Their father fixed it.
What did the old lady say?
She said, "Hey, look at these animals!"
What did Max want to prove?
He wanted to prove that he was a big boy.
How many houses did they manage to visit?
They managed to visit 15 houses.

lessons.title: A List for the New Year
lessons.summary: On the last night of the year, Sam writes a list of ways to improve his life, then makes it shorter.
lessons.text:
It was the last night of the year. Sam was at home with his sister, Ann. They had a tradition. Every year, before the beginning of the new year, they sat down at the table and wrote a list.

"The beginning of a year is a good opportunity," Ann said. "It's an opportunity to change something."

Sam decided to write a long list. He wanted to improve many things. He started writing.

"1. Improve my health. 2. Reduce my time on the phone. 3. Read one book every month. 4. Find a new career. 5. Reduce my coffee to one cup a day. 6. Watch only one episode of a TV show each night, not five."

Sam kept writing. After half an hour, he had written 20 things. He looked at everything he had written. Then he realized something. "This list is too long," he said. "I can't do all this."

Ann looked at the list. "You're right," she said. "Choose three. Three things are enough."

Sam decided to keep only three things. He wanted to improve his health. He wanted to look for a new career, because he did not like his job. And he wanted to watch only one episode each night.

At 11, they watched one episode of their favorite show. Then, at 12, they went outside and looked at the sky. "Happy New Year!" said Ann. Sam was happy. He was ready for the new year.

Questions:
What did Sam and Ann do every year?
They sat down at the table and wrote a list.
What did Ann say about the beginning of a year?
She said it was a good opportunity to change something.
How many things had Sam written after half an hour?
He had written 20 things.
What did Sam realize?
He realized that his list was too long.
How many things did Sam keep?
He kept only three things.

lessons.title: Goodbye, Mrs. Brown
lessons.summary: On the last day of school, a class gives their teacher a book of letters for her last year.
lessons.text:
Mrs. Brown was a teacher. She started in this school district 35 years ago. Her subject was history. This year was her last year at the school. After the summer, she was going to stop working.

At the school, there is a tradition. On the last day of school, each student writes a letter to the teacher. This year, Mrs. Brown's class wanted to do something bigger. They wanted to make a book for her.

Each student wrote one section of the book. Each section was one page. In his section, Leo wrote about his favorite history class. In her section, Mia wrote about the day Mrs. Brown helped her with a hard test. Every student was an author. The class put the name of each author on his or her section.

On the last day, the class gave the book to Mrs. Brown. She read the first section, then the second section. She was very happy. "Thank you," she said. "This is a beautiful book."

Then she showed them an old file. "In this file, I keep letters from my students," she said. "Some are from 30 years ago. This book is going to be my favorite thing in the file."

Before the students left, Mia asked, "Can we stay in contact with you?" Mrs. Brown wrote her address on the board. "This is my address," she said. "Please write to me. Let's stay in contact."

Questions:
What was Mrs. Brown's subject?
Her subject was history.
When did Mrs. Brown start in the district?
She started in the district 35 years ago.
What did each student write?
Each student wrote one section of the book.
What does Mrs. Brown keep in her old file?
She keeps letters from her students.
What did Mrs. Brown write on the board?
She wrote her address on the board.

lessons.title: The Island Party
lessons.summary: Nora and her parents visit a small island in the north for its yearly party for the sea.
lessons.text:
In August, Nora and her parents visited a small island. The island is in a region far in the north. There is no bridge to the island. The only access is by ship. The trip on the ship took one hour.

They went to the island for a special event. Every August, the people of the island have a party for the sea. The sea is very important in this region. For a very long time, the people of the island worked on the sea.

On the first morning, an old man gave a tour of the island. Nora and her parents joined the tour. The tour started at the old church and ended at the water. The man talked about the culture of the island. "Our culture comes from the sea," he said. "Our songs are about the sea. Our food comes from the sea."

Later that day, the party started. People played various old songs, and they danced in the street. There were various kinds of fish to eat. Nora tried a little of everything.

At night, everyone walked to the water. They put small lights on the sea. The lights moved on the water. It was very beautiful.

Nora's father looked at the sea and the lights. "For me, this is the most beautiful place on earth," he said. Nora agreed. "The most beautiful place on earth," she said.

Questions:
Where is the island?
The island is in a region far in the north.
What is the only access to the island?
The only access is by ship.
What did the old man talk about on the tour?
He talked about the culture of the island.
What did people do at the party?
They played various old songs and danced in the street.
What did Nora's father say about the island?
He said it was the most beautiful place on earth.

lessons.title: A Surprise for Mom
lessons.summary: Kate and her father plan a surprise birthday dinner for her mother at a French restaurant.
lessons.text:
Kate is 12. Her mother loves French food. She lived in France for a year when she was young. In May, Kate and her father decided to plan a surprise for her mother's birthday.

There is a very good French restaurant in the city. But there is a lot of demand for tables there. "The demand is very high on Friday and Saturday nights," her father said. "Perhaps we can get a table on a Thursday." He called the restaurant a month before. He talked to the manager. The manager was very nice. "We have a table for three on Thursday at 7," the manager said.

On Thursday, Kate's father said to his wife, "Let's go for a walk in the city." Her mother did not know about the surprise. They walked to the restaurant. "Surprise!" said Kate. "Happy birthday, Mom!" Her mother was very happy. "What a nice surprise!" she said.

Their table was not ready, so they waited at the bar. Her father had a coffee at the bar, and Kate had some water. After 10 minutes, the manager came. He directed them to a table by the window. "Please follow me," he said, and he directed them through the room.

The food was very good. Her mother spoke French with the manager. "Perhaps this is my best birthday ever," she said. Kate and her father were very happy. The surprise was perfect.

Questions:
What food does Kate's mother love?
She loves French food.
Why did Kate's father call a month before?
He called because there is a lot of demand for tables.
Who did Kate's father talk to?
He talked to the manager.
Where did they wait?
They waited at the bar.
Where did the manager direct them?
He directed them to a table by the window.
